debt_events.summary: Entered privately negotiated exchange agreements for approximately $15.0 million principal amount of remaining 0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 at 96% of face value, initially issuing 1,097,444 shares and potentially up to 848,265 additional shares based on the VWAP true-up.

Completed the 2025 exchange offer: 97.44% of the 2027 Notes were tendered and accepted, with $209.721 million aggregate principal amount of 7.00% Convertible Senior Secured Second Lien PIK Toggle Notes due 2030 and 317,834,446 new shares issued; the transaction was accounted for as a troubled debt restructuring.

Entered a Loan and Security Agreement for a delayed-draw term-loan facility of up to $100.0 million; $40.0 million was drawn on 2025-06-26 and $60.0 million on 2025-09-18. As of 2026-06-27, $110.9 million including accrued PIK interest was outstanding and no amount was available to borrow.

The company reported compliance with the 2030 Notes and Loan and Security Agreement covenants as of the quarter-end date; the agreements include a $15.0 million minimum-liquidity covenant and a $60.0 million cap on cash used to repay the 2027 Notes at maturity, subject to stated exceptions.

A federal court entered a $15.4375 million judgment against Beyond Meat in the Sonate trademark case, consisting of $37,500 actual damages and $15.4 million disgorgement; further motions or appeals were possible.

distress_signals.summary: The latest quarter had an 8.2% year-over-year revenue decline, a $30.8 million operating loss and a $27.7 million adjusted EBITDA loss; the company also reported negative operating cash flow of $23.2 million for the six months ended 2026-06-27 and said it expects to continue operating at a loss for the foreseeable future.

Management concluded disclosure controls were not effective because two previously identified material weaknesses remained unremediated: accounting for non-routine and complex transactions, and inventory valuation/data integrity.

As part of the Global Operations Review, Beyond Meat ceased operational activities in China at the end of 2025 and was winding down the facility and lease; the filing also describes workforce reductions, product-line exits and further manufacturing/real-estate footprint optimization as part of its cost-reduction program.

Following the full-time start of COO Brijesh Krishnaswamy on 2026-09-30, interim Chief Transformation Officer John Boken stepped down from that role effective 2026-10-07, with responsibilities reassigned to the COO and other senior leaders.
The $15.4375 million trademark judgment is an additional legal cash obligation and remains subject to possible further motion practice or appeal.

ownership.value: Publicly traded company (NASDAQ: BYND). Millennium Management LLC, Millennium Group Management LLC and Israel A. Englander reported beneficial ownership of 957,442 shares, or 5.2% of the class, under Schedule 13G; the filing was not made to influence control.

output.risk_rationale: Beyond Meat has substantial debt relative to its latest-quarter revenue, remains loss-making with negative operating cash flow, and has already used a troubled-debt exchange and additional equity-for-debt exchanges to manage maturities. The company says it was covenant-compliant and expects existing cash plus anticipated operating cash flows to fund the next twelve months, but weak demand, unremediated material weaknesses, no available delayed-draw capacity, a recent $15.4375 million judgment and ongoing leadership/footprint changes make counterparty risk high. Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1655210/000165521026000055/bynd-20260627.htm and https://investors.beyondmeat.com/node/14616/html.
